speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Massage Establishments Act regulates massage establishments, by licensing the operators and imposing conditions on their activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The aim is to prevent massage establishments from being used for vice activities or causing law and order problems.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has reviewed the massage establishment regulatory regime to ensure that it remains effective in the changing landscape.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Under the enhanced regime, we will take tougher action against unlicensed massage establishments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many of these were not, in fact, massage establishments but fronts for vice activities, the proverbial "wolf in sheep’s clothing" or what in Chinese we refer to as "挂羊头卖狗肉".

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For licensed massage establishments, we will take a more calibrated approach.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, we have about 1,200 licensed massage establishments that are sited both within residential and non-residential areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: About 300, or one quarter, are found in Housing and Development Board (HDB) housing estates.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: They include reputable massage establishments that have been operating for a long time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The evidence is that there is a clear difference between licensed and unlicensed massage establishments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In 2016, Police enforcement found less than 3% of licensed massage establishments to have vice-related infringements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is significantly lower than the 40% of unlicensed massage establishments with vice-related offences.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Even as we tighten the regulations on higher-risk activities and take stricter and more punitive action against errant operators, there is room to lighten the regulatory burden for the vast majority of low-risk and compliant operators who are meeting a genuine demand for massage services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This differentiated approach will also allow the Police to focus its resources accordingly.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Given the substantial amendments to the Massage Establishments Act, MHA will repeal the existing Act and re-enact it.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: All existing licences granted under the current Act will continue to be in force, but they will be treated as granted under the new Act, and subject to the new regulatory regime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: I will first explain the provisions to strengthen the Police’s levers against unlicensed massage establishments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will use a combination of measures to more effectively deter and penalise those who are involved in unlicensed massage establishment operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Today, the penalty for unlicensed massage establishment operations is a maximum fine of $1,000.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is grossly insufficient compared to the profits that unlicensed massage establishments can make, especially by engaging in vice activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The significantly higher fines and the inclusion of imprisonment as a punishment will be a stronger deterrent.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If the unlicensed massage establishment also engages in vice activities, the operator can be liable for additional vice-related offences under the Women’s Charter.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The enhanced penalties will ensure that unlicensed massage establishment operators face serious consequences upon conviction.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, Court proceedings take time, especially if the unlicensed operator claims trial.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There have been cases of unlicensed operators blatantly continuing to operate even after being charged in Court, due to the lucrativeness of their illegal activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This power will be used if the Police have reasonable grounds to suspect that despite ongoing criminal proceedings, the operator continues to operate the unlicensed massage establishment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The premises closure order will require the unlicensed massage establishment premises to be vacated within a specified time and physically secured thereafter.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If the order is not complied with, the Police is empowered to take necessary steps, or use reasonable force, to enforce the closure of the premises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Under clauses 20 and 21, any person who breaks the lock or enters the premises without prior permission from the Police will be deemed to have breached the order.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This person could face a maximum fine of $15,000 or three years' imprisonment or both.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The premises closure order is intended to only prevent the continued operation of illegal activities and will not penalise usage of the premises for legitimate businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clause 19, therefore, sets out the circumstances under which the order will be lifted.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In addition, under clause 22, the accused may appeal to the Minister against the Commissioner's premises closure order, but the order will remain in force during the appeal process.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Bill will also deal with the upstream problem of irresponsible landlords who knowingly lease their premises to unlicensed massage establishment operators.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will require landlords to evict tenants who have been convicted of unlicensed massage establishment operations and provide them with early notice.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Police will notify the landlord when their tenant is charged in Court for operating an unlicensed massage establishment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This is a legal requirement under clause 28.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Landlords will, therefore, have no reason to be unaware of their tenants’ illegal activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: After the tenant has been convicted of operating an unlicensed massage establishment, under clause 29, the landlord must require the tenant to hand over possession of the premises within a month.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There is typically some time between the tenant being charged in Court and conviction.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As such, the early notification under clause 28 will give landlords sufficient lead time to make the necessary preparations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We recognise that some tenants could be difficult to deal with and may not leave despite the landlord’s request.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: In these cases, the landlord is expected to take the following steps to discharge his obligations under the Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Thereafter, if the tenant still refuses to move out, the landlord should apply to the Magistrate’s Court for a summary order for the delivery of possession of the premises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: There will be penal consequences for the tenant if he refuses to vacate the premises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If the landlord has taken these steps, he will have fulfilled his obligations and no action will be taken against him.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Otherwise, the Police will take action against the landlord for the offence of allowing his premises to be used for operating an unlicensed massage establishment under clause 5.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This offence carries the same penalties as the offence of operating an unlicensed massage establishment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The second set of amendments will refocus the regulatory regime on higher-risk activities and reduce the regulatory costs on low-risk activities and compliant massage establishments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: At the same time, we will enhance levers and powers available to the Police to deal with the errant massage establishment licensees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The current definition of "massage or special treatment" under the Massage Establishments Act includes manicure, light treatment for hair removal, fish spas and baby spas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Such activities do not pose the same law and order concerns as traditional massage establishments offering body massages in private rooms.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will reduce the regulatory costs for such businesses.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: However, if any person provides massage services under the guise of such low-risk activities, they will face the increased penalties for unlicensed massage establishment operators.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We will also introduce a suite of measures to keep unsuitable persons out of the massage industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Under the current regime, the Licensing Officer assesses the fitness and propriety of an applicant or licensee when deciding whether to issue or revoke a licence.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Under clauses 7 and 12, MHA will expand this assessment to include other "relevant persons", besides the applicant or licensee, who can influence the decisions of the business.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: These "relevant persons" include the "responsible officers" of the business entity as defined in clause 2, and all persons with substantial interest in, or have control or direction over, the business.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: If the applicant, licensee or "relevant persons" are not fit and proper, the Licensing Officer can refuse to issue a massage establishment licence and revoke an existing one.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will reduce the risk of massage establishments being started or operated by persons who are unfit or improper but are hiding behind a veil of propriety.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Police will publish the criteria and requirements for applicants, licensees and "relevant persons" on their website at a later date.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Examples of these serious offences include vice-related offences under the Women’s Charter, as well as offences relating to trafficking-in-persons and organised crime.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This allows the Police to take immediate action to prevent the licensee from using the massage establishment premises for such serious crimes, without having to wait for the potentially lengthy Court proceedings to be concluded.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The licensee is also required to seek the Licensing Officer's approval before hiring an employee.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Not doing so will be an offence under clause 13.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Employees who are not fit and proper will not be allowed to work in a massage establishment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The fit and proper criteria for massage establishment employees will be set out in the subsidiary legislation at a later stage.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, if any employee has any involvement with vice activities, or has been convicted of serious offences, such as outrage of modesty, he or she will not be allowed to work in the massage establishment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The licensee or employee may appeal to the Minister against the Licensing Officer’s decision, but the decision will remain in force pending the outcome of the appeal.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: We have also enhanced the Police’s powers to take swift and effective action against errant licensees.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clause 10 creates a new provision to allow the Licensing Officer to modify licence conditions, in order to intervene promptly against problems and disamenities associated with massage establishments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, if a licensed massage establishment poses law and order problems, the Licensing Officer may decide to curtail its operating hours for the remaining duration of its licence term.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clause 10 prescribes the process for modifying licence conditions, which is straightforward and I will not go into here.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Police have encountered cases where massage establishments lock their doors to obstruct or delay enforcement.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clause 24 empowers Licensing Officers and Police Officers to enter massage establishment premises using necessary force and without a warrant, if there is reasonable suspicion that offences under the Act are being, or have been, committed within.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clause 4 of the Bill allows the Licensing Officer to appoint suitably-trained individuals, such as Auxiliary Police Officers or retired Police Officers, as "authorised persons".

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: This will provide the Police with deployment flexibility and allow them to conduct more frequent checks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Authorised persons will be empowered under clause 23 to enter and inspect massage establishment premises.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Under clause 26, authorised persons can request for records, accounts and other information relating to the massage establishment for purposes of compliance checks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Authorised persons, however, will not be given the more specialised powers that the Licensing Officer and Police Officers have, for example, powers of investigation and the new power of forced entry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Clause 30 protects Licensing Officers, Police Officers and authorised persons from personal liability, as long as they have acted in good faith and executed their duties with reasonable care.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: As part of the review, MHA consulted the Spa Association Singapore, the Spa and Wellness Association of Singapore and the Real Estate Developers’ Association of Singapore on the proposed amendments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The industry associations and their members are supportive of the proposals under the Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Bill allows tougher action to be taken against unlicensed operators and errant licensees, who damage the image of the massage industry.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Many of these are, in fact, not massage establishments but fronts for vice activities, the so-called "wolf in sheep's clothing".

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Bill will provide the Police with more levers to tackle these unlicensed massage establishments in several areas.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: Past cases have shown that licensed massage establishments have a lower tendency for vice activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The Bill will focus on regulating higher-risk massage activities and introduce several new measures.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: For example, to ensure that licensed massage establishments are operated by a suitable person, the Police will not only assess the fitness and propriety of the applicant or licensee, but also other relevant persons who are in a position to influence the operation of the massage establishment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: The proposed amendments will strengthen MHA's regulatory framework for massage establishments.

speaker: The Second Minister for Home Affairs (Mrs Josephine Teo)
text: (In English): Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: While massage establishments can provide valuable health-enhancing services, we cannot shy away from the fact that many have been used as a facade for carrying out vice-related enterprise.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The media have covered this: 19 June 2016, the New Paper reported, "Dhoby Ghaut Spa Almost like a Brothel"; 8 June 2017, Asiaone reported, "Police Raid Five Massage Parlours for Illicit Activities"; 29 August 2017, The Straits Times reported, "79 People Arrested for Offering Sexual Services at Massage Parlours, Gambling and Working without Permits".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The higher regulation embedded in this Bill is needed to target the recalcitrant massage establishments.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: By taking a less regulated approach to businesses offering manicures, pedicures and the like, the Police are now able to productively deploy and focus resources to clamp down on parlours which are mere shopfronts for vice activities.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I hope this law will encourage the Police to prioritise their anti-vice raids on suspicious parlours within residential areas.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I have had a complaint of a suspicious parlour along Bukit Timah Road within the constituency I serve, close to schools and homes.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As the Police prioritises their anti-vice raids, I would hope officers will first focus on rooting out vice activities near residential areas.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Allow me, Mr Speaker, Sir, to speak of certain aspects of this Bill.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If a person re-offends in the same manner, he or she can face a heavier punishment.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Under this order, it is no longer up to the person being charged to decide whether or not unlicensed activities are going on at the massage establishment.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The premises can be locked up, secured and disused.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Thirdly, this Bill adds a duty on owners or occupiers to ensure that a person deliver up the premises within one month after conviction of certain offences.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Through enhanced punishment, a premises closure order and the determination of a lease, this Bill ensures that massage establishments are robustly regulated.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I note that there has been a change of rule-making power conferred by this Bill.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Under section 13(2b) of the current Massage Establishment Act, the Minister could make rules concerning "the standards of hygiene to be observed in establishments for massage".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This does not appear under clause 35 of this current Bill before the House.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The general clause for rule-making, which is clause 35(1), would probably not extend to hygiene since the only other health-related provision is that of clause 35(2c), a prohibition against employing a person who has not "undergone and passed a medical health screening if required to do so by a licensing officer".

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Therefore, I stand in strong support of this Massage Establishment Bill.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: It is timely to strengthen our laws and regulations to protect genuine massage establishments and penalise those that use this as a cover for vice activities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This sends the correct signal that we are serious in tackling this problem.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We also need to go further to weed out all parties that are responsible for letting such businesses thrive.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: We need to establish stricter rules on landlords, especially those operating within the heartlands.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Besides the guise of massage establishments, there are news reports of those using traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) centres as a guise for sexual offences.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can MHA consider working with the merchant associations to strengthen our intelligence collection against such illegal establishments?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: What other mechanisms are there in place for HDB to obtain feedback on establishments that flout the rules?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Is there a debarment period before these people could operate similar businesses again?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Perhaps it might be useful to limit their operating hours as some of them operate even till midnight.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Does the Ministry have any plans to revise these requirements and make it even stricter for massage establishments that want to operate in HDB heartlands?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: With regard to Part 6 clause 28, it seems to suggest that the premises owner is liable only if he or she knows that the place is being used as a massage establishment without a licence.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Does this liability extend to sexual and other vice activities done at the premises, which is a breach of the licensing conditions?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Does the Ministry have enhanced levels of punishment for multiple infractions?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Can we consider the forfeiture of tenancy, especially if it is a commercial space in an HDB estate?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Could some kind of penalty be imposed on the landlords who repeatedly have such establishments operating on their premises, but still evict and take reasonable steps to evict the operator within a month?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: Could restrictions be placed on advertisements of massage establishments in the heartlands?

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: All stakeholders need to play their role, especially landlords, who cannot adopt a rent-and-forget approach anymore.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
text: This Bill sets it in the right direction.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The proliferation of massage outlets in our HDB and residential estates is of significant concern for many residents.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For example, one can spot five massage establishments in a row at just one block in an HDB neighbourhood.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I really cannot see the basis for such concentration of massage establishments in our HDB estates.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Residents are concerned that such outlets can be used as fronts for illicit vice activities, resulting in law and order and social problems.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: There have also been complaints about the suitability of advertising materials featuring half-naked women displayed prominently on shop fronts, which operate 24 hours a day.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Many outlets make misleading claims about the efficacy of their massage treatments, with the "menu of services" offering lymphoma detox, kidney-care treatment, ovary-care treatment and so on.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For example, one spa promotes their "Royal Prostate Package", offering customers two hours of "Prostate Care therapy".

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The advertisement boasts “comfortable and serene environment, exquisite and professional technique will bring your health to new heights”.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: It also adds: “Let our young, pretty and experienced masseuses bring back your energy, vitality and loosen up your pressure!!” I think that doctors in this House may agree that the implied service is probably not to treat urological disorders.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Massage establishments should follow clearly prescribed guidelines on the use of suitable promotional images and messages.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This is especially important where the outlets are located near schools and in residential areas.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Therapists should not be scantily clad when working, but instead be clothed in proper attire, including uniforms, in order to promote a healthy image for the industry.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The Government should also consider banning hard-sell tactics and touting of massage services outside massage establishments.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Passers-by should not be harassed by such practices, especially in busy HDB town centres and tourist sites.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: I would also like to ask the Minister what is the rationale for allowing massage establishments to operate 24 hours a day.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: Given the risk of massage establishments being used as fronts for vice activities, which often involve foreign therapists, I would like to ask the authorities to carefully calibrate the fit and proper criteria for granting approval for massage establishment employees.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: To ensure transparency of such licensing, all approved employees should be issued with an identification (ID) or certificate that should be prominently displayed at the outlet.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: This will help identify "approved" employees more easily and help prevent unlicensed masseuses from working illegally.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: For approval to be granted, employees must meet minimum qualifications for the services they are licensed to provide, including passing a therapist code of conduct that clearly spells out the "dos" and "don'ts" with clients and the penalties for breaches.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: However, this will only be effective through determined enforcement of the new powers.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: So, I urge the authorities to take decisive action to eradicate unlawful activities.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The authorities should monitor these low-risk outlets and ensure that the vice operations are not simply conducted under a different banner.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
text: The industry can be repositioned with a more positive image and realise their potential to provide good and meaningful jobs for Singaporeans, including the visually handicapped.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, it is necessary to increase the penalty for illegal massage establishment operators.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The current penalty of less than $1,000 is, indeed, too low.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I also urge the Minister to disallow those operators to register any beauty or wellness businesses, and forbid foreigners who have been proven to be involved in vice activities to enter Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We must strengthen our control and supervision because these beauty or wellness establishments can easily be converted into places for illegal activities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They are often involved in various criminal activities and become the centre for spreading venereal diseases and other diseases, threatening our social security and national health.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There are many shops providing beauty and wellness services and the Police cannot conduct frequent checks on all of them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Strict registration rules can help weed out suspicious operators from the beauty and wellness industries and it is a preventive and deterrent measure.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Another thorny issue is that there are more and more illegal massage groups operating in residential areas.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Both HDB and the private estates are facing the same challenge.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Recently, the Police have successfully raided illegal massage parlours and brothels.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The operators, hence, turn to HDB flats and the private condominiums to continue with their illegal activities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: (In English): The heart of the problem is really vice and related illegal activities.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am in favour of the heavier penalties which are overdue.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Measures, such as closing unlicensed premises during criminal proceedings and penalising landlords who knowingly continue to lease their properties, are well and good.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My concern is: how do we deal with the operators who move into residential areas?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have been receiving complaints from a number of my residents who had complained to me about this recurring problem in their estates.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Many of such workers enter Singapore as visitors.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How do we nab the illegal workers who may not have gone for the necessary health checks?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I do realise that to remain a dynamic and vibrant city, we have to maintain open borders.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, we must also devise strategies to deter and keep out undesirable visitors.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I look forward to hearing the deterrent measures the Ministry has in place.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I conclude with my support for the Bill.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, I would like to seek some clarifications.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: However, to adapt from the well-known Police advisory – low-risk does not mean no risk.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: During my time in the Police Force, I have seen hair salons, manicure salons and other supposedly "low-risk" establishments being used as a cover for vice activities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: So, I would like to ask: how does the Ministry plan to prevent such allegedly low-risk outlets from engaging in vice once they are exempted from licensing?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is important that landlords play their part in ensuring the activities that are being carried out on their premises are legitimate.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They want to know how would the authorities determine whether landlords knowingly or unknowingly lease their properties to tenants who engage in vice activities.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can the Ministry clarify on the investigation process and explain the parameters that would determine the landlord's culpability?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There is also the perennial issue of the tenants – the licence applicants being set up as the fall guy.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How does the Ministry intend to deal with the same mastermind who works behind the scenes, operating various unlawful massage establishments under the guise of different applicants?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And if it was a case of a low-risk massage establishment being used as a front for vice activities, the authorities should consider making it necessary for any subsequent similar outlets to require a licence before operating from the same premises.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This would help to deter the same undesirable activities from taking place in the premises and prevent a vice hotspot from taking root.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such outlets, as some of my other Parliamentary colleagues have said, are usually a magnet for vice activities and attract various unsavoury characters.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This can cause much unhappiness and threatens the social compact between residents and tenants.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Worst still, in a Strata Title, there is not much that can be done to deter a defiant landlord.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would, therefore, like to urge the Ministry to minimise the number of massage establishments in mixed-use developments.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Next, I would like to touch on the importance of uplifting the negative perception of the massage industry.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would the Ministry consider working with the relevant agencies to provide Workforce Skills Qualifications (WSQ) training for all masseuses, and consider professional certification to be a mandatory aspect in the application for a massage establishment licence?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Professional certification would certainly help to ensure that those working in the industry are well-trained, and this will help in uplifting the industry's image.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: In addition, stiffer advertising guidelines should also be implemented for massage establishments, such as on social media channels, where we can easily find advertisements for massage services which carry suggestive messages and accompanied by pictures of improperly clothed ladies.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Under the provisions in the Bill, licensed massage establishments with good track records will be given a longer licence period.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can the Ministry give a clearer definition of what constitutes a good track record?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Perhaps, the Ministry can explore including professional certification of masseuses as part of what a good track record should be.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, I support the Bill.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What about the so-called masseuses who provide non-massage services?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Landlords who take "reasonable steps to do so will not be penalised", states the Bill.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Could the Second Minister elaborate on the term "reasonable steps" and what it will constitute?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This is a welcome move but I would like to further urge the Minister to take one step further to confiscate properties used for vice activities if the landlord is found complicit in the activities at the conclusion of the investigation.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have seen a proliferation of reported TCM establishments operating as tui-na or massage centres, some with rather dubious operators.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As such TCM clinics are not registered with the Ministry of Health, is this a potential loophole for such operators?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Also, there are many such massage establishments in plain sight.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In fact, many are advertising openly in tabloids online and many are still operating, despite this open knowledge.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This will have a greater deterrent effect on those who operate massage establishments as fronts for prostitution, vice and other illegal activities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The approach taken in this Bill mirrors the changes made to the Public Entertainment Act in May this year.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I take this opportunity to comment on and seek clarifications on four areas of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: First, I seek clarification on the ambit of the matters that the licensing officer may take into account to decide whether or not to grant the licence under clause 7 of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: One specific issue that has arisen in my constituency is the concentration of massage establishments within a relatively small area, a point that the hon Members Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Melvin Yong made as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: All of these establishments are in close proximity to residential areas.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the past year, there were four applications to open new massage parlours.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: One 24-hour spa has since closed due to Police enforcement action.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: My residents are appreciative of the close monitoring enforcement on these establishments by the Police.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: However, they are naturally concerned that there should not be a proliferation of such establishments as there is the potential for the character of their neighbourhood to change.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Planning Act provisions referred to in clause 7(3)(d) and (e) of the Bill are not necessarily engaged as these establishments operate from HDB shophouses.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I would be grateful if the Minister could please confirm that the licensing officer would be able to take into account factors, such as the character of the neighbourhood and concentration of existing massage establishments under clause 7(7) of the Bill, in deciding whether or not to grant new massage establishment licences as well as to restrict the hours of operation of the massage business.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: If so, given that the Police are basically a law enforcement agency, may I please ask how the licensing officer would be able to get reliable inputs on these factors?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: A connected practical issue concerns the liaison between HDB and the Police.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: From time to time, HDB would be approached for written permission to change the use of HDB shophouse premises of which it is the head lessor to that of a massage establishment.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Last year, on noting that HDB has issued written permissions for conversion of several shops into massage parlours in Bukit Batok, I suggested that HDB coordinate these efforts with the Police to establish a workflow in relation to such matters, obtain relevant inputs and then make the necessary assessment before issuing written permission.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: With a well thought out workflow, there is potential to cut down redundant steps and make it user-friendly for the applicants, too.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: One specific issue that I wish to ask is whether the Police would process an application to operate a massage establishment at an HDB shophouse before an applicant obtains written permission from the HDB to effect the change of use.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Would the Police take the cue from HDB or vice versa?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In my personal view, issues, such as concentration of massage parlours within HDB shophouses in a particular area, may equally be considered and handled at HDB's end with inputs from the Police through the lever of written permission.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In this way, the problem can be nipped in the bud.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I would be grateful for the hon Second Minister's view on the preferred approach to be taken.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Second, I note that under clause 32 of the Bill, the Minister has powers to exempt any premises from applying for a licence.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Exemptions are also granted for premises where certain forms of massage, such as traditional massage, are administered in full view of the public.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Does the Ministry intend that these exemptions will continue under the regime introduced by this Bill?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Additionally, I am aware that the Ayurvedic Practitioners Association Singapore has long sought for exemption status to carry out Ayurvedic massages of their patients which, for practical purposes, cannot be done in full view of the public.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Is there an intention to extend exemption status to other forms of curative massage?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Third, I note clause 5(2) of the Bill prohibits any person from advertising or representing that he or she provides massage services in an establishment for massage unless the person holds a valid licence to do so at the premises.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The Public Entertainment Act also has a similar provision.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: It is provided in section 12 of the Public Entertainment Act that the licence issued by the authorities must be prominently displayed at the premises.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This statutory requirement does not appear to be reproduced in this Bill.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The advantage of such a requirement are twofold.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I would recommend that the Minister consider imposing a similar requirement under this Bill requiring operators to prominently display the licence or instrument conferring exemption status at massage establishments.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Notwithstanding the queries I raised, I agree with the need for our authorities to exert greater control over massage establishments.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: While this is necessary as a deterrent, it is even more important to step up enforcement with more effective checks and frequent raids on such outlets.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For buildings with a higher concentration or recurrence of seedy providers, is it possible to require them to install closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras along the corridors and entrances to help deter illegal activities?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: They should be required to submit evidence of periodic surprise checks, at least twice a year, to prove their diligence in ensuring that their properties are not being used for illegal activities.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Only certified personnel will be allowed to practise in such massage establishments, and practitioners may face revocation of their licences if breaches are made.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This body will also regulate and protect the employment rights of the practitioners, coordinate and provide training and upgrading programmes.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With that, I conclude with my support for the Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These are sentiments which are echoed by netizens who posted comments on my Facebook page.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Mr Zain Kazmi said, "Singapore's reputation has been diminished by the operation of such sleazy businesses.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We cannot afford to allow such vices to continue unabated, as it tarnishes the name of genuine massage parlours and the country at large".

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was my first impression when I read this Bill and started drafting the speech.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: However, as I looked into it and researched further and met with the sex workers themselves and with Project X, a non-profit which provides social, emotional and legal support for sex workers in Singapore, I realised that the amendments here are just part of the equation.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: It is only tackling the supply side and not the demand.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The other part of the equation that we are not tackling in this Bill is equally important.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I do understand that the Ministry of Education's current Sexuality Education programme already has elements to mitigate youth paying for sexual services.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I feel there is more we need to do and, perhaps for a start, launch a detailed study and research to understand this demand before we can come up with further legislative and policy amendments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If we do not address the root of the problem, we will always be one step behind.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We are now clamping down on massage establishments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the demand continues, which I am quite sure it will, the vice activities will just move on to the next place.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: We already know from media reports that sexual services are offered at some TCM clinics.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The current amendments do not cover TCM clinics and perhaps this is where the vice activities at massage establishments will be heading.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Of course, we can then legislate again and cover TCM clinics.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I hope Members see where I am heading.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: And if there is demand for something, there will always be supply.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Worse still, we might drive these activities further underground.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This was the fear of former Home Affairs Minister Mr Wong Kan Seng who said this in Parliament in 1999 in relation to a question about prostitution, "And it is better that the Police know where these areas are and enforcement action can be taken, rather than to disperse these brothels to the whole of Singapore and we then have a cat-and-mouse game chasing after them or, worse still, drive them underground, and they will be operating everywhere." Minister Wong also said, “Criminalising prostitution will only drive such activities underground, resulting in crime syndicates taking control over such activities.” And I wonder whether crime syndicates have taken control of some of these unlicensed massage establishments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Do some of these unlicensed massage establishments have links to other criminal elements and activities by organised criminal syndicates which finance the presumably high initial set-up costs of such massage establishments?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Again, a detailed study will allow us to further understand the underlying complex ecosystem driving this trend of the growing number of unlicensed massage establishments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: As I mentioned earlier, I met up with the sex workers – Singaporean sex workers.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I met a young Singaporean who has been a sex worker for two years and is also currently pursuing her diploma.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She uses the money earned to pay for her education and is intending to pursue her degree as well and is saving up for that.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I met a single lady who is a sex worker to help pay for her parents' medical fees.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I went into that meeting with an open mind to listen and to try and understand their viewpoints.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: To listen to their concerns and the dangers they faced working as a sex worker and how they worry about their safety.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I listened to how lonely they felt at times, working in this industry.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: At the end of the day, there is no quick fix, no easy solution.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But the way forward is for us to study this issue holistically and engage all the parties concerned.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This is a complex issue and I hope that this Bill is a start, and we can look into this issue much further.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In my following speech, I would use the term "massage workers" to refer to masseuses who provide a happy-ending service in massage parlours.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Based on the Ministry's press statement, the Bill's primary intent seems to be to eliminate vice from massage parlours.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The logical extension of this would be that the Bill's secondary intent is to force massage workers to leave the trade.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: However, this would pose a few problems and questions.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It is clear that, historically, it is impossible to eradicate vice from any society.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The Member Mr Baey Yam Keng was quoted in The Straits Times in 2010 saying that the raids of Geylang have led to vice spreading out into the neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The same article quoted an ordinary citizen saying that Geylang is very quiet now compared to the past.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In the past few months, newspaper headlines have been dominated by the raids on brothels in HDB estates, unlicensed massage parlours and fake TCM practitioners.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Separately, in the past, there used to be these health centres where sexual services were provided alongside massage.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Most of these health centres were not allowed to renew their licences.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The shutdown of these health centres led to the proliferation of smaller parlours set up by the people who used to work at these health centres.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: From interviews with massage workers, the proliferation was also because smaller parlours were harder to apprehend for sexual services.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Massage workers provide sexual services due to their personal circumstances and, to them, it was the most viable way to earn a substantial living through their own labour and to support their families.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Project X, which hon Member Mr Louis Ng mentioned, is a local non-government organisation (NGO) that works with sex workers to ensure their safety, physically and emotionally.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: They have spoken to many Singaporean massage workers doing this for anything between two years and 30 years.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The one thing they have in common is that they do not possess the sort of educational qualifications that are privileged in the society we live in, and a job anywhere else would be one with long hours and little pay.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: And, importantly, transition into a job where they can earn a commensurate amount of money in order to successfully support their family?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Thirdly and correspondingly, through the experience of Project X, I have come to understand that, for many, it is immensely hard to leave the trade but there are amazing success stories of women leaving that industry.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: There are many factors that determine that: a supportive family, good business and finance acumen, will power and opportunities all played a part in that.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In the face of criminalisation, stigma and occasional violence, it creates a series of setbacks, disempowering them.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: That said, this is based on the assumption that all massage workers want to leave their jobs.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We know of women who have done this for most of their lives and absolutely cannot imagine anything different.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: To be clear, these women do not want to be dishonest or break the law.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I will quote some of them who said, "We want to apply for licence but we cannot.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Without a licence, we cannot apply for Central Provident Fund (CPF).

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We have worked here for seven, eight years".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Even the Thai worker is also Singaporean, married to Singaporean but her husband does not want her anymore and she has to work and look after the children.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: There is another one I spoke with who has five kids; she had no place to live, so she lives in those backpacker hostels.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We had to buy Maggi noodles for her.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: But now, she has finally found a place to live and it is because she does this job that can help her to support her children.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Echoing her voice, another massage worker shared that "Those working here are Permanent Residents (PR) or citizens.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: I myself have two kids and have to support them.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: My husband earns $1,800 a month as an electrician.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: He works from 8.00 am to 5.00 pm.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: After work, he goes to the childcare centre and picks up my kids.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: But I work here at night to earn money for the family".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: A common theme among many of the women was that they all felt that they would not be doing this kind of work if they did not have to.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Many do this so that their children can have a bright future, one that will hopefully be starkly different from their own.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: These women are textbook cases of the woman who sacrifices for her children.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: One of the massage workers who was also her own boss said, "Our business here does not affect others.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: We operate here which is common for this line of business and not in housing areas nor close to schools.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Being a PR or citizen, the money we earn stays in this country and it is spent on our family and children who will grow up and contribute to the country in the future.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Without much qualifications, this is the only industry we can work in.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: It is not committing crime, we never "杀 人 放 火 " or set fire or kill.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Deputy Speaker, Sir, in the past, there was a common understanding that we all did what we needed to do to survive.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I have been working with the authorities, the multi-agency task forces and the anti-vice department for at least a dozen years now.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I am quite happy with the results that I have gotten in Geylang.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I stand in support of the Bill, Mr Deputy Speaker.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: I have several issues and clarifications to make.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: With this Bill, we are dealing with an industry that requires enhanced regulation and stricter enforcement.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It is not going to be a walk in the park because of the multitude of factors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: As all the nine speakers before me have shared, there are many, many issues, indeed, to be considered.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: For one, just look at the types and numbers of massage available currently – body massage, manicure and pedicure-related massage, chiropractic light massage, electric massage, vapour massage and other baths-related massage, foot reflexology, slimming massage, spa services, head massage, traditional massage, curative massage, and even physiotherapy massage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: It is thus becoming a lot easier to actually have non-approved and illegal activities under the guise of some of these services because it is so wide-ranging.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: As all applications and approval for licences are regulated, does the authority have the ability to regulate the number of such premises that are allowed within certain areas?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: For example, I have come across seven such premises within one and a half blocks located near a private residential area and a secondary school.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: And mind you, this is not in the Geylang lorong vicinity; it is up north in my constituency, therefore, the concern from the residents in the vicinity.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Seven premises within one and a half blocks?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Should there be better coordination and oversight of this?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: In fact, Mr Deputy Speaker, with this Bill, I still do not see this being addressed specifically, thus, my concern.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: On the Police licensing website, it is clearly written that massage establishments, some of them are not regulated by the Massage Establishments Act.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Perhaps, these are the establishments that may go negative.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Can we actually monitor these and, perhaps, they should also come under the oversight and regulation of this Bill?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Also on the website, I note that a foreigner is eligible to apply for a Massage Establishment licence as long as he holds a valid Work Permit or Employment Pass.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Should the Ministry be reviewing this as well, as they may actually open up a can of worms, perhaps something else may come about, especially when some of our foreign friends may open TCM centres in the guise of providing massage.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Pertaining to the term "fit and proper person" in Part 2, clause 7.4, I understand the licensing body will look out for certain criteria.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: However, of greater concern is that the persons who are not fit and proper or have been blacklisted before, may apply for the licence through a third party, a family member or a friend.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Once the licence is granted, that is when the problem starts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The modifications happen, the partitions will come up, and the operations at the premises can go off course, and the illegal way, of course.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are there innovative ways to circumvent and stop this problem from happening?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: This is actually one of the problems that we are facing in some of the establishments.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: One suggestion would be to have regular and conscientious follow-up and checks on these premises on a more sustainable basis.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: One of the Members who spoke earlier mentioned perhaps twice a year.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: What is the number of such establishments operating in Singapore currently?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Also, numbers like repeat offenders as these are usually of concern to us as well.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: As there are plans for the Ministry to work with the trade associations for the beauty and wellness industry, with this upcoming implementation of the Bill, they may actually form partnerships to assist with increased compliance and understanding as well as assist with some level of surveillance, I feel.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Are there specific steps that the Ministry is going to implement pertaining to this?

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The beauty and wellness industry, Sir, is an interesting and dynamic one.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: Whilst there are many kosher operations which benefit the health of many in a variety of ways, there are some bad apples circulating and using the industry for their own needs and illegal activities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
text: The clean-up requires collaborative efforts by parties concerned and stepped-up, organised and conscientious enforcement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They have raised many useful points which I will try to address.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Several Members raised concerns about massage establishments in residential areas, including Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Melvin Yong and Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef, who rightly pointed out that it is not a walk in the park.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Christopher de Souza said that the Police should prioritise anti-vice enforcement efforts in residential areas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Murali Murali asked whether the Police will engage relevant stakeholders in deciding whether to grant new massage establishment licences and take into account land use considerations when assessing licence applications.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo suggested working with merchant associations to strengthen intelligence on illegal establishments and gathering feedback on licensed massage establishments that flout the rules.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: MHA understands and shares the underlying concerns of our Members.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun said that "massage worker" refers to masseuses who provide happy-ending services in massage parlours.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He added that under the current Act, massage establishments can continue to operate even when they have been fined for being non-compliant.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Massage workers can earn a living without providing sexual services.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is the first thing we have to acknowledge.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Not all masseuses are trying to provide additional services.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I will state categorically also that when it comes to vice and other illegal activities in massage establishments, the Police have zero tolerance, especially in residential estates.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Police and HDB take all feedback, all complaints from residents and the community seriously.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will assess each feedback and take necessary actions to enforce our laws.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To mitigate the risks of vice and disamenities due to massage establishments, the Police take a much stricter licensing approach for massage establishments in residential areas, compared to those that operate outside residential areas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The agencies will assess the suitability of the location.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will not allow new massage establishments in an area if the existing massage establishments are problematic and pose law and order issues, so we do not add to the problems.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The agencies will also assess whether the proposed massage establishment will cause disamenities to the surrounding areas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In residential areas, we take into account feedback from the community.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will ensure that the various agencies' processes are fully coordinated.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are not as coordinated as they need to be now.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But clause 7(3) of the Bill now makes that a requirement, clearly specified.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, as some Members have noted, licensed massage establishments in HDB estates must obtain what is known as a Category I licence under the Police licensing framework.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Such criteria help to ensure that the applicants are bona fide operators who have put in the effort and investment to run legitimate massage businesses.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Thirdly, the Police impose specific conditions to reduce the potential disamenities from massage establishments in residential areas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Foo Mee Har gave suggestions on more stringent licensing conditions that could be imposed on massage establishments situated within residential estates.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Several of these are already in place today.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For instance, employees of licensed massage establishments are required to wear uniforms that are approved by the Licensing Officer.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is approved and if you are not wearing the uniform, you have breached the licensing condition.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, if you know of any instance where someone is not dressed appropriately, that cannot be an approved uniform, let us know.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are also prohibited from touting for business outside the massage establishment premises.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo and Ms Foo Mee Har asked if the Ministry would consider limiting the operating hours of massage establishments located in housing estates.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This applies to licences granted or renewed since August this year.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Under clause 10 of the Bill, the Licensing Officer will be empowered to modify existing licence conditions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, the restricted operating hours will be fully implemented for all licensees within HDB estates after the re-enacted Act comes into force.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, if you are in an HDB estate, once this new Bill comes into force, the limited, curtailed operating hours will apply.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo, Ms Foo Mee Har and Mr Melvin Yong highlighted concerns about inappropriate advertisements by massage establishments and urged the Ministry to subject massage establishments to advertising guidelines.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Police intend to impose a new licensing condition to prohibit licensees from displaying indecent advertisements.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will need some time to work out the specific details but the intent is clear, advertisements will have to be within certain guidelines.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked about the number of licensed massage establishments within residential estates with vice-related infringements, and whether they will be allowed to operate massage establishments in future.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If a massage establishment has vice-related infringements, the licensee will no longer be considered fit and proper to hold a massage establishment licence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Licensing Officer will revoke the massage establishment licence, and he will not be granted a new massage establishment licence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked about the number of unlicensed massage establishments in Singapore.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But so as not to cause undue alarm, let me clarify that the vast majority of these unlicensed massage establishments were found in non-HDB properties.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: A relatively small 7% of the unlicensed massage establishments were found in HDB properties.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To say it another way, most unlicensed massage establishments were not in HDB properties and most licensed massage establishments in HDB properties did not have vice infringements, less than 3%.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, we should not assume that all of them are somehow involved in vice.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Louis Ng asked about the Police's enforcement plans against such unlicensed massage establishments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will not tolerate such errant operators that exhibit a flagrant disregard for the law.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Where specific feedback is received about suspected unlicensed massage establishments and their illegal vice activities, the Police will assess the information and take necessary actions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Police naturally have to work within their resource constraints, but the intention is to maintain the enforcement pressure against unlicensed massage establishments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To share with Members, in 2016, on a monthly basis, Police carried out more than 100 enforcement checks, more than 100 every month.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This Bill will provide the Police with the levers to act more effectively against the unlicensed massage establishments which take up a lot of time.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Louis Ng cautioned that "low-risk activities" do not mean "no-risk".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They are worried that these are not required to obtain massage establishment licences and yet, they could still be fronts for illicit massage or vice activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The situation today is not quite like this, except for a very small number of bad hats.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As I shared in my opening speech, vice activities are far more prevalent in unlicensed massage establishments, not even in those that are exempted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We may be reducing regulatory costs for bona fide operators but they would not be getting a free pass to use their businesses as a facade for something else.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If a business purports to be providing low-risk services like manicure and pedicure but, in effect, is offering massage services, it will have to apply for a licence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And if it fails to do so, the business will be treated as no different from any other unlicensed massage establishment and penalised.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Joan Pereira asked whether the revised fines for unlicensed massage establishments would serve as sufficient deterrence, given the lucrativeness of their illicit activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We are adopting a suite of measures, as Mr Christopher de Souza puts it, that gives the "extra teeth necessary" to clamp down on unlicensed massage establishments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And more than that, the offenders can now face imprisonment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Second, should an unlicensed massage establishment continue to operate even after the operator has been charged in Court, the Police can order the closure of premises.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Third, we will go upstream to tackle the supply of premises, by taking irresponsible landlords to task if they knowingly lease their premises to unlicensed massage establishment operators.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked if harsher penalties can be imposed on the landlords who repeatedly have such establishments operating on their premises.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Joan Pereira also said that convicted unlicensed massage establishment operators should be disallowed from subsequently operating any beauty salons or health centres, given the ease with which these premises can be reconfigured for illicit vice activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You tell us that you want to operate a massage establishment and your track record is that you had been non-compliant, you had been convicted before, you are not "fit and proper".

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If they offer massage services without a licence, then the same penalties as operating an unlicensed massage establishment applies, even if they call it a beauty salon or a health centre.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It does not matter what they call it.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will look at what actual activities are taking place.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But if Ms Pereira is suggesting that they be prevented from operating a bona fide beauty or health business, for example, doing facials or selling organic supplements, then from a Yellow Ribbon perspective and also considering the comments by Mr Kok Heng Leun and Mr Louis Ng, that may be going too far.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Some Members spoke on tackling vice more generally, beyond massage establishments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Joan Pereira is concerned about the possible displacement of vice activities to residential areas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: She raised concerns that many of these vice workers are foreign nationals who have entered Singapore as visitors, and suggested that entry bans be imposed on foreigners involved in vice-related activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Kok Heng Leun asked about the Ministry's plans to ensure that vice does not happen where we do not want it to.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Alex Yam also asked about action that can be taken against masseuses found to be providing illegal sexual services.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The Police keep a close watch on the vice situation in Singapore and will not hesitate to take the necessary enforcement actions to stamp out vice activities that spring up in residential areas.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In cases where the Police have received complaints and detected brothels in HDB flats, the Police will also investigate the owner of the flat.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
