text: The Police will also notify HDB, which will then take stern action if the flat owner is found to have misused his flat, including imposition of fines, and possibly, compulsory acquisition and debarment from buying another HDB flat.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Louis Ng and Mr Kok Heng Leun talked about the personal circumstances of Singaporean sex workers.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But for providing sexual services in a massage establishment, the person will cease to be fit and proper and will no longer be allowed to work in a massage establishment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: For those who wish to transit to other types of work, I appreciate it really may not be easy for them, but help is available and we are most willing to reach out to them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They will be removed from Singapore and may not be allowed to re-enter.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Alex Yam and Mr Gan Thiam Poh sought clarifications about the proposal to punish landlords who knowingly lease their premises to unlicensed massage establishment operators.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I have addressed these points earlier in my speech.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In summary, a landlord will know about the charge against his tenant through the Police’s notification.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The landlord would not be in a situation that he is caught unaware.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Once a person is charged, we will inform them.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: After the tenant has been convicted of operating an unlicensed massage establishment, the landlord must require the tenant to hand over possession of the premises within a month.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Thereafter, the Bill allows the landlord to terminate the lease without any contractual liability.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If the tenant still refuses to move out, the landlord should apply to the Magistrate’s Court for a summary order for the delivery of possession of the premises.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And if the landlord takes these steps to evict the tenant, the Police will not take action against him.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Melvin Yong, Mr Alex Yam and Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested imposing additional obligations on landlords, such as placing the onus on landlords to proactively check whether their tenants have massage establishment licences, putting in place sanctions on premises that have been used for vice activities, or confiscating such properties.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do expect responsible landlords to check whether their tenants have valid massage establishment licences, both before and during the tenancy agreement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: However, we must also recognise that this is not always possible.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There could be mala fide unlicensed massage establishment operators who mislead the landlord into believing that the premises will be used for legitimate businesses.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Other tenants may decide to operate a massage establishment midway through its tenancy agreement, without first informing the landlord.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In such cases, it will not be fair to penalise the landlord.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But bear in mind that egregious landlords can be imprisoned, which is likely a stronger deterrent than any sanctions on the property.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Desmond Choo asked if the provision to penalise landlords who knowingly lease their premises to unlicensed massage establishment operators can be extended to premises with licensed massage establishments that are involved in vice activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: He also asked whether termination of tenancy can be considered if the premises is an HDB commercial property.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In holding landlords responsible, we try to strike a balance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: If the landlords have done their due diligence by leasing the premises to only licensed massage establishments, it may not be fair to take them to task for something that occurs within the licensed massage establishments which they are genuinely not aware of.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In addition, as I have shared in my earlier speech, the incidence of vice in licensed massage establishments is significantly lower than that in unlicensed massage establishments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: As such, the main problem that this provision seeks to tackle is that of irresponsible landlords who have contributed to the problem of the increase in unlicensed massage establishments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Nevertheless, if unlawful vice activities are detected within HDB commercial properties, HDB can take action to terminate the tenancy.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Melvin Yong and Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef raised the point that persons who are not "fit and proper" may apply for the licence via a third party, such as a family member or friend with a clean record.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Clause 7 of the Bill seeks to address this by expanding the assessment of licensee suitability to other "relevant persons" in the business.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This seeks to prevent errant operators from hiding behind clean applicants to continue to operate massage establishments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But Members who have been in law enforcement know how difficult it can be to detect persons who deliberately hide.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: At least with this provision, the Police is clearly empowered to act to reject an application if they suspect that it is being made by a bad hat operating behind the scenes.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This will empower the Police to say that they suspect this is not a clean applicant and someone is hiding behind this.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The law says that the Police can now reject the application, whereas previously, it was left unsaid.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef also surfaced concerns that after the licence has been granted, there may be illegal operations at the premises.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Licensed operators who run afoul of the law will face increased penalties under the Bill.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh suggested that massage establishments in buildings with a higher concentration or recurrence of seedy massage establishments be required to install CCTVs along the corridors and entrances to deter illegal activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Clause 10 of the Bill will allow the Police to modify licence conditions to address this concern.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Should licensed massage establishments pose law and order problems, the Police can intervene quickly and impose additional licensing conditions.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: One such condition could be the installation of CCTV cameras to deter crimes in and around the massage establishment and to facilitate investigations into any such crimes that take place.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Murali Pillai and Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef asked whether we will consider a demerit points system for massage establishments, similar to that for the public entertainment licensing regime.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Repeat offenders also face the risk of imprisonment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is stricter than the demerit points system – one strike and you could be out.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Murali Pillai said that all licensed massage establishments should be made to display their licences, which would serve as a deterrence against the operation of unlicensed massage establishments and provide some form of consumer protection.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, under the licensing conditions, massage establishment licensees are already required to prominently display the massage establishment licence within the premises to ensure that patrons and inspecting officers can easily identify licensed massage establishments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Failure to comply with this requirement is a breach of the licensing conditions, and licensees will face stiff penalties under the updated regulatory regime.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: What I can also share with Members is that, in fact, the Police have taken operators to task for failing to display their licences.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Ms Foo Mee Har, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Gan Thiam Poh said that all masseuses hired at licensed massage establishments should meet minimum professional qualifications.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, in deciding whether to grant a massage establishment licence or to grant written approval for an individual to work in a massage establishment, the Licensing Officer already considers whether the employee possesses the necessary recognised qualifications or certifications.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: This is made clear in clauses 7(3) and 15(1) of the Bill.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In other words, not anyone is allowed to work in a massage establishment.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: There are "fit and proper" criteria, and an assessment of the employees' qualifications.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Of course, if they do not have those, the operator will have committed a breach and we take them to task.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Melvin Yong asked for a clearer definition of what constitutes a "good track record" that will entitle the licensee to a longer licence validity period.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: By "good track record", we refer to compliant operators without any adverse records or infringements over several years.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked whether existing exemptions will continue under the updated regulatory regime.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Alex Yam asked if TCM services will be covered under the Bill, while Mr Louis Ng mentioned that the current amendment does not cover TCM clinics.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We will continue to exempt massage establishments that are assessed to be providing low vice-risk activities.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: These include outlets where treatment is personally administered by a registered medical professional.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, if you have a shop front that says TCM clinic, you go inside, the practitioner has got a registration under the TCM Practitioners' Act that is issued by the TCM Board and that practitioner personally administers the treatment, that can be exempted.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: You can see everything that is going on in the premises.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: That is what is known as open-concept massage establishments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Mr Murali Pillai asked about curative as well as Ayurvedic treatments.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They cannot say, "We do not want a licence.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: They need to get a licence because it is not open-concept, we cannot see what is going on.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef suggested that we work with the industry trade associations for the upcoming implementation of this Bill.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But as Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef reminded us, it is really not a walk in the park.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Members know from what I said earlier – advertising, requirements, some of the other licensing conditions – all of these we will have to proceed to implement.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But with the support of the House, Mr Deputy Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: The first point I would like to clarify is that in my speech, I did not intend to say all massage workers are actually providing sexual services.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I made in the context of the speech what I wanted to talk about.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: And exactly what I said was, "In my following speech, I would use the term 'massage workers' to refer to masseuses who provide a happy ending service in massage parlours".

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: So, it is within the context of my speech.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: So, if there is any misunderstanding, I would clarify that and say sorry to those who felt that what I said have caused injustice to them.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: The second point is that I am glad to hear that MHA would like to engage sex workers to help them.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I would also urge the Ministry to work with the NGOs with regard to that.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: I can help to do the bridging if need to.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: Thirdly, I just want to hear MHA's response to this because, from my research on this issue, a lot of time, the men who go to the massage parlour, the male clients, they, in fact, expect such so-called "happy services" from the masseuses.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: And sometimes, they may even coerce that to happen.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: What will MHA be doing in such a situation in order to protect the masseuses as well as the massage parlours?

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I would like to give that assurance.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I have two outstanding queries for the Second Minister.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: On the concern about concentration, why do we find eight massage establishments in HDB estates within, like three minutes' walk?

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I hope the Ministry would encourage that diversity and limit the number of establishments per HDB precinct, just like Minister Khaw Boon Wan had done for foreign workers renting HDB flats.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: I think that was a very effective measure.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: So, if the Second Minister could consider that.

speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har
text: And that is the common complaint that comes from residents.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In this way, we have already curtailed the number of massage establishments in each residential area while allowing legitimate and well-run massage establishments to operate.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: To impose a limit or a quota, you need a number and it will be arbitrary.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Each residential area has different characteristics, residents and businesses, as the Member correctly pointed out.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Whatever number is set, it could still be too high for some areas, for example, if it is right next to a school.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Unless that number is zero, which means then this quota is zero.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We can also end up in a situation where there is an argument about how big the trade radius ought to be for this number to be applied.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: In some areas, 200 metres, very sparsely populated; in some areas, 200-metre radius, a lot of people staying there.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is not quite so cut and dried, not so straightforward to determine a number; not so straightforward to determine what the trade radius is.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We do not particularly want to see so many massage establishments around even if they are licensed.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, I think that those measures are available to the Police.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Then, to the Member's second question about the employees.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, that is why the requirement is placed on them to display the licence and not on the individual employees.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: We accept the fact that, actually, in all kinds of businesses, employees come and go.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Today, you may have one staff, she has worked here three months; another day, you may have another who has just joined.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: The more important thing is that the operator takes his licence seriously and ensures that no one who is not licensed works there.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, even if a person wears a badge and so on, it is not possible, it is not so easy for the individual customer to determine the validity of that employee's pass.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: But the enforcement officer is in a stronger position to decide whether the licence is valid or not.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: Just wearing any tag does not actually give us that much protection and reassurance.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: And the Member pointed out that Mr Wong had talked about this 20 years ago.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: I am quite sure even 20 years from now, there will still be vice activities that we will have to tackle in different forms.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: So, it is always going to be a challenge.

speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
text: It is always something that we have to keep learning to tackle more effectively.
